read: Healthcare worked as a defensive trade last week. XBI rose about 4% and IBB about 5%, while QQQ fell about 2%. On Friday, as Nasdaq 100 dropped 3.5% on a tech sell-off, Iran tension and pre-midterm nerves, European healthcare gained 2.4%. Q3 results showed a clear split. Immunology franchises (Dupixent, Skyrizi/Rinvoq) and Regeneron delivered beats and guidance raises. Alnylam showed how quickly a growth story re-rates when pricing policy (the 340B change) and competition collide. Big pharma is turning savings into pipeline money: AZ's $1.5bn programme follows GSK's. Sanofi and AbbVie both signalled appetite for M&A, with Sanofi now open to larger late-stage or commercial deals. For a Monday the deal tape was quiet. Fresenius and WuXi Biologics agreed a 37-candidate biosimilars option deal, the IPO window stayed open (Bambusa upsized, Aspen priced at the low end) and Tuesday's midterms are the macro overhang.

items.headline: Regeneron gains about 12% on a clean Q3 beat
items.detail: Revenue was $5.1bn, up 36% and well above roughly $4.6bn consensus. Global Dupixent sales reached $6.5bn (+35%), US Eylea HD $699m (+62%) and US Libtayo $550m. Eylea HD is finally offsetting Eylea erosion, and an FDA decision on cemdisiran in gMG is due in November.

items.headline: Alnylam falls about 25% as the TTR franchise stalls
items.detail: The TTR franchise made $1.15bn in Q3 (+59% y/y), but the CFO steered FY26 to the low end of $4.7–5.1bn, signalled no Q4 growth and pushed 2027 guidance to February. Truist estimates 15–20% of Amvuttra volume is exposed to the 340B change on 1 Jan 2027, and BridgeBio and Pfizer are taking share. The stock is down 56% YTD (about $23bn market cap), and Oppenheimer names Sanofi the likeliest bidder.

items.headline: Sanofi raises FY26 guidance again and opens the door to larger M&A
items.detail: Q3 sales were €14.44bn (+14.3% CER) against €13.25bn expected, and Dupixent made €5.69bn. FY sales growth guidance rises to low teens and EPS growth to mid teens. Shares closed up about 6%, the highest since April. The CFO is now willing to go beyond the usual $2–5bn deal size toward late-stage or marketed assets, with roughly €20bn of capacity. He also said Sanofi would launch in Europe at higher prices under MFN rather than withhold launches.

items.headline: AstraZeneca launches a $1.5bn annual savings programme; the call points to R&D cuts and trials moving to emerging markets
items.detail: The programme carries up to $2bn in one-off charges and should be largely complete by end-2029, with savings reinvested in oncology, cell therapy and AI. Q3 revenue was $16.2bn (+7%) and core EPS $2.79 (+17%). Oncology made $7.8bn (+17%), while Farxiga fell 25% to $1.6bn on US generics. FY guidance is confirmed, and the ADR rose about 7% on Friday.

items.headline: AbbVie raises FY26 EPS guidance and signals bolt-on deals
items.detail: Q3 sales were $17.4bn and EPS $3.82, both above consensus. Skyrizi grew 23% to $5.7bn, and the FY Skyrizi outlook rises to $21.8bn, the third raise this year. Rinvoq grew 24% to $2.7bn, while Humira fell 31%. FY EPS guidance moves to $13.95–13.99, the dividend rises 5.2%, the stock is at all-time highs and the CEO is steering toward bolt-ons rather than another Allergan-scale deal.

items.headline: Inovio wins its first approval: Voceryq (INO-3107) gets accelerated approval in adult RRP
items.detail: The shares rose about 257% after hours, and Precigen (Papzimeos) fell about 27% after hours. Voceryq is a plasmid DNA immunotherapy delivered with the CELLECTRA device, and the 12-month complete response rate was 27% (7/26 evaluable). A confirmatory trial is required. Orders are expected in about 60 days, with full launch in Q1 2027.

items.headline: Acumen falls about 80% as sabirnetug fails Phase 2 ALTITUDE-AD; its only asset is dropped
items.detail: The oligomer-selective Aβ antibody showed no separation from placebo at 18 months on the primary endpoint or any key secondary, and ARIA-E occurred in about 10% of patients. Acumen is cutting cash burn and reviewing strategic options. It is another negative data point for the soluble-oligomer hypothesis.

items.headline: Agios: FDA extends the PDUFA for mitapivat in sickle cell disease by three months, to 1 Feb 2027
items.detail: Agios's REMS-related safety update (about nine months of RISE UP open-label data) was classified as a major amendment. The REMS question carries over from liver injury seen in thalassaemia, though Agios says it has seen no similar hepatocellular cases in SCD.

items.headline: Gilead/Kite: partial clinical hold on next-generation CAR-T trials after ICANS cases
items.detail: The hold affects KITE-753 (bicistronic CD19/CD20, rapid manufacture) after several cases of neurotoxicity. Lymphoma CAR-T is Kite's in-house growth bet beyond Yescarta.

items.headline: Fresenius signs an exclusive option deal with WuXi Biologics on up to 37 biosimilar candidates (Monday)
items.detail: The deal would take Fresenius Kabi's portfolio from 29 to as many as 66 molecules, with originator sales above €370bn in scope. WuXi works fee-for-service for each candidate selected, and Fresenius keeps global rights and the full economics. The first targets are polatuzumab vedotin and teprotumumab, and FY26 guidance is unchanged.

items.headline: IPOs: Bambusa (BBTX) upsizes to $169m and Aspen Neuroscience (ASPE) raises $140.6m; both began trading Friday
items.detail: Bambusa priced at $16 (midpoint) on about 10.5m shares; its lead, BBT001, is an IL-4Rα×IL-31 bispecific for AD. Aspen priced at the low end ($15); it develops autologous iPSC dopaminergic cells for Parkinson's, with OrbiMed, ARCH and Gilead as holders. That takes 2026 biotech IPOs to about $8bn across 29 deals.

items.headline: Biotech outperforms in a risk-off week: IBB +5%, XBI +4%, XLV +3% against SPY −0.6% and QQQ −2%
items.detail: On Friday European healthcare rose 2.4% while Nasdaq 100 fell 3.5%, with Brent near $110 on Iran risk and US midterms on Tuesday. Rotation into defensives is supporting large caps more than the long tail.

items.headline: Molecular Partners cuts up to 44% of staff (up to 55 roles) to focus on radiopharma
items.detail: Cash was CHF 57.5m at 30 Sept, with runway into late 2027.

items.headline: Setara raises $90m to advance a TRPV4 inhibitor spun out of Jazz's Actio deal
items.detail: Indications are CMT2C and overactive bladder; investors were not disclosed.

items.headline: Immutep cuts staff after the Phase 3 efti futility stop
items.detail: Cash was about $34.1m at 30 Sept, with runway into H1 2028.

items.headline: Moleculin completes dosing in Part A of the pivotal MIRACLE trial (annamycin, AML)
Alkermes starts a Phase 2 of ALKS 7290 as adjunctive treatment in MDD
Repligen launches a $1bn convertible notes offering to extend debt maturities
